in order for fault tolerance schemes in applications to be able achieve high reliability with low performance penalty, the fault tolerance schemes in the applications need to be adaptive to system environments.
in order to achieve a high reliability and high performance, applications need to adapt their fault tolerance schemes to different system environments.

1) the fault tolerance scheme used for high performance parallel and distributed computing should be application adaptive; and 2) an application should choose a fault tolerance scheme that is near optimal for the platform it is executing with.

the following issues: (1) What kind of fault tolerant schemes can and should be used in applications; (2) What kind of system information should be collected and what kind of fault tolerant scheme is appropriate for a given system environment; (3) What is the impact on the performance of applications when different fault tolerant schemes are incorporated in the applications; (4) What kind of adaptive method can be applied to achieve high reliability and high performance for applications.

The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the future, fault tolerant applications need to be designed in a self adaptive way so that the applications can achieve the highest possible reliability under whatever system environment they run with as low performance overhead as possible.
the performance of an application is often more sensitive to the choice of fault tolerant schemes than to the choice of parallel algorithms.
